title: Coordinate derivatives of absolutely convergent monomial series
statement:
Fix an integer $m\geq0$ and positive real numbers $R_1,\ldots,R_m$. For multiindices $\alpha\in\mathbf N^m$ put $R^\alpha=\prod_iR_i^{\alpha_i}$, $z^\alpha=\prod_i z_i^{\alpha_i}$, and $\alpha!=\prod_i\alpha_i!$. Let $a:\mathbf N^m	o\mathbf C$ satisfy $\sum_\alpha |a_\alpha|R^\alpha<\infty$, with absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] and sums interpreted as limits of finite subsums. On $P_R=\{z\in\mathbf C^m:|z_i|<R_i\}$ define $F(z)=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha z^\alpha$. For every $
u\in\mathbf N^m$, the iterated ordinary complex coordinate derivative $\partial^
u F$ exists on $P_R$ and
$$\partial^
u F(z)=\sum_{\alpha\geq
u}a_\alpha rac{\alpha!}{(\alpha-
u)!}z^{\alpha-
u}.$$
Here $\alpha\geq
u$ means coordinatewise inequality, and derivatives can be taken in any order with $
u_i$ derivatives in coordinate $i$. For every positive $s_i<R_i$, the series on the right converges absolutely and uniformly on $|z_i|\leq s_i$. In particular $\partial^
u F(0)=
u!a_
u$. When $m=0$ these assertions mean $F=a_0$ and the only derivative is order zero.

proof.text:
For $m=0$, the multiindex set has just its empty index, every weight and factorial is $1$, and the domain is a point. The assertion is exactly $F=a_0$. Assume henceforth $m>0$. Put $b_\alpha=|a_\alpha|R^\alpha$ and $B=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha<\infty$. For each $
u$ define $h_{\alpha,
u}(z)=a_\alpha\alpha!z^{\alpha-
u}/(\alpha-
u)!$ when $\alpha\geq
u$, and $h_{\alpha,
u}=0$ otherwise. In particular $h_{\alpha,0}=a_\alpha z^\alpha$.

proof.text:
The nonnegative family $C_{
u,s}b_\alpha$ is summable, since multiplication by a constant commutes with each finite subsum and its limit. Apply [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] to obtain absolute convergence of $\sum_\alpha h_{\alpha,
u}(z)$ at every point of the closed smaller polydisc. Apply [lem-wf-dominated-continuous-function-series] to both the terms and their absolute values for uniform convergence: enumerate $\mathbf N^m$ by increasing total degree, lexicographically inside each finite degree. This enumeration exhausts every finite subset, so the finite-subsum hypothesis gives a summable sequence of the same bounds. The cited uniform convergence of initial sums also gives uniform convergence of the net of all finite subsums: beyond an initial segment, every omitted or extra finite tail has norm bounded by the sum of the same nonnegative tail, which tends to zero. Write the resulting sum as $H_
u$; in particular $H_0=F$.

proof.text:
For a coordinate $j$, fix all other coordinates. Each function $w\mapsto h_{\alpha,
u}(z_1,\ldots,w,\ldots,z_m)$ is a scalar monomial or zero. By [lem-sfb-complex-monomial-derivative] its derivative is $h_{\alpha,
u+e_j}$. Indeed, if $\alpha\geq
u$ and $\alpha_j>
u_j$, the power rule multiplies the coefficient by $\alpha_j-
u_j$, giving $\alpha!/(\alpha-
u-e_j)!$. If $\alpha_j=
u_j$, its power in $w$ is zero and its derivative is zero. If $\alpha
ot\geq
u$, both the function and its required derivative are zero.

At $z=0$ a term of $H_

u!a_
u$, including $
